data.title: Resource Hijacking for Cryptomining
data.summary: The sample consumes host CPU, GPU or cloud compute resources for the operator's benefit — most commonly cryptocurrency mining — degrading legitimate workloads and, in cloud environments, generating direct billing impact.
data.description:
Unlike most impact techniques, the damage here is ongoing and resource-proportional
rather than a single destructive event: a miner left running accrues cost and performance
degradation for as long as it is undetected, which in a cloud environment translates
directly into a compute bill rather than only a performance complaint. Mining processes are
typically throttled to stay under a threshold that would trigger obvious user complaints
while remaining profitable.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on sustained anomalous CPU/GPU utilisation attributable to an unrecognised process, rather than only on peak usage that a throttled miner may deliberately avoid.
* In cloud environments, check for unexpected compute-instance scaling or billing anomalies as a parallel detection signal independent of host-level telemetry.
* Terminate the mining process and check for an associated persistence mechanism — a throttled miner is usually built to survive a reboot and resume.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on sustained anomalous CPU/GPU use even below peak, and check cloud billing for scaling anomalies.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Ran a throttled cryptomining routine capped at 60% CPU utilisation, re-launched via a scheduled task on reboot.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Mining workload was throttled to avoid triggering obvious performance-complaint thresholds.
